concepts.title: Circumference of Circle
concepts.definition: The circumference of a circle is the total length of its boundary. It is the distance covered in one complete round along the circle.
concepts.formula: C = 2 * pi * r, where r is the radius of the circle and pi is approximately 22/7 or 3.14
concepts.key_idea: Circumference is the perimeter of a circle, directly proportional to its radius.

concepts.title: Area of Circle
concepts.definition: The area of a circle is the total region enclosed by the circle. It measures the space inside the circular boundary.
concepts.formula: A = pi * r^2, where r is the radius of the circle
concepts.key_idea: The area of a circle is proportional to the square of its radius.

concepts.title: Length of Arc
concepts.definition: The length of an arc is the distance along the curved part of a circle between two points. It is a fraction of the circumference determined by the central angle.
concepts.formula: l = (theta / 360) * 2 * pi * r, where theta is the central angle in degrees and r is the radius
concepts.key_idea: The arc length is the fraction theta/360 of the full circumference.

concepts.title: Area of Sector
concepts.definition: A sector of a circle is the region enclosed by two radii and the corresponding arc. The area of a sector is a fraction of the area of the circle determined by the central angle.
concepts.formula: A = (theta / 360) * pi * r^2, where theta is the central angle in degrees and r is the radius
concepts.key_idea: The area of a sector is the fraction theta/360 of the total area of the circle.

concepts.title: Area of Segment of Circle
concepts.definition: A segment of a circle is the region between a chord and the corresponding arc. The area of a segment is found by subtracting the area of the triangle formed by the chord and two radii from the area of the sector.
concepts.formula: Area of segment = Area of sector - Area of triangle = (theta/360) * pi * r^2 - (1/2) * r^2 * sin(theta)
concepts.key_idea: The segment area equals the sector area minus the triangular area formed by the chord and the two radii.

solution_steps.explain: Triangle = (1/2) r^2 sin(theta) with the same two radii.
Segment area = sector area minus triangle area.

worked_examples.solution: Sector area = (90/360)*(22/7)*14*14 = (1/4)*616 = 154 sq cm. Triangle area = (1/2)*14*14 = 98 sq cm. Segment area = 154 - 98 = 56 sq cm

concepts.title: Area of Combination of Circular Regions
concepts.definition: The area of a combination of circular regions is found by adding or subtracting the areas of individual circles, sectors, or segments depending on how they overlap or combine.
concepts.formula: Total area = Sum of individual areas (with appropriate addition or subtraction for overlaps)
concepts.key_idea: Break down the combined figure into simple circular regions and compute each area separately, then combine.

worked_examples.question: Find the area of a shaded region in a square of side 14 cm with four quadrants of radius 7 cm at the corners.
worked_examples.solution: Area of square = 14*14 = 196 sq cm. Area of 4 quadrants = 4 * (90/360) * (22/7) * 7 * 7 = 4 * (1/4) * 154 = 154 sq cm. Shaded area = 196 - 154 = 42 sq cm

worked_examples.question: Find the area of a leaf-shaped region formed by two quadrants of radius 7 cm each inside a square.
worked_examples.solution: Area of one quadrant = (90/360)*(22/7)*7*7 = 38.5 sq cm. Two quadrants = 77 sq cm. Square area = 49 sq cm. Leaf area = 77 - 49 = 28 sq cm

concepts.title: Area Between Two Concentric Circles
concepts.definition: The area between two concentric circles (circles with the same center but different radii) is the region enclosed between the outer and inner circles. It is found by subtracting the area of the inner circle from the area of the outer circle.
concepts.formula: Area = pi * R^2 - pi * r^2 = pi * (R^2 - r^2), where R is the outer radius and r is the inner radius
concepts.key_idea: The area between concentric circles is the difference between the outer and inner circle areas.

concepts.formula: Sector area = (theta/360)*pi*r^2; Segment area = Sector area - Triangle area
